solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Bribe to lie in court or snub screws

indicators.note: screws as a verb means twists or contorts, so the letters of the two words beside it are wrenched into a new order

explanation.surface: A crooked fixer either bribes a witness or snubs them by turning the screws.
explanation.walkthrough: 'screws' is the anagram signal working on OR SNUB.
explanation.definitionFit: To suborn is to induce someone, usually by bribery, to commit perjury or another wrong.

clue.text: Reaping-hook old Sicilian mentioned

indicators.note: mentioned means spoken of, so the word for the old Sicilian is to be heard rather than read

parts.note: a Sicel was a member of an ancient people of Sicily

explanation.surface: A farm tool once named by an ancient islander.
explanation.walkthrough: The Siceli (Sicels) were an early people of eastern Sicily; their name is pronounced like the curved blade.
explanation.definitionFit: A curved blade on a short handle for cutting corn is a reaping-hook, the same tool by another name.

clue.text: Russian composer could make do with …

indicators.note: could make means could be formed from, so the letters named are reassembled into a new word

parts.note: the dots carry on into the next clue, whose answer supplies a five-letter bird

explanation.surface: A Russian composer could get by with whatever follows.
explanation.walkthrough: The trailing dots link to 3 Down: its answer, the songbird, joins DO and the seven letters are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Alexander Borodin, composer of Prince Igor, was a nineteenth-century Russian, one of 'The Five'.

clue.text: … dressin' bird that can sing

definitions.meaning: robing means dressing in robes; clipped as 'dressin'', it loses its final G
a small red-breasted songbird common in British gardens

explanation.surface: A bird in its finery is given a voice.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe in 'dressin'' shows a dropped G: ROBING without its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The redbreast is a familiar songbird, so a singing bird describes it by example.

clue.text: Tufts College as Poe described it

indicators.note: described is taken as drawn out in a new shape, so the letters given are arranged afresh

explanation.surface: A writer of macabre tales depicting a New England university.
explanation.walkthrough: The blogger read 'described' as 'went round', C inside the rest; either way 'it' is padding.
explanation.definitionFit: Scopae are the brush-like tufts of hairs on the legs of bees used for gathering pollen.

clue.text: Under belly of aircraft powdered snow is at first drifting. It may delay flight

indicators.note: a belly is the central part, so the middle letters of the word for the plane are taken
powdered means crushed into fine grains, so the letters after it are broken up and reformed
at first means the opening letter of the word it qualifies

explanation.surface: Snow blowing beneath an aeroplane holds up its departure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Under' just places the rearranged letters after the belly of the aircraft; 'drifting' gives only its first letter, though it looks like the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A strong side wind across a runway can make take-off unsafe, holding departures back.

clue.text: Wicked for example and in Paradise Lost originally dreadfully queer

indicators.note: dreadfully means badly or awfully, so the letters with it are mangled into another order
originally means at the start, so the opening letters of the two words of the poem's title are taken

explanation.surface: Musing that the musical Wicked and Milton's epic both seem odd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dreadfully' rearranges P and L (first letters of 'Paradise Lost') with QUEER.
explanation.definitionFit: The musical Wicked tells what happened before The Wizard of Oz, so it is an earlier-set companion story.

clue.text: Substitute bitter vetch at first sign of zoogonidia

parts.note: ers is the name of the bitter vetch, a leguminous plant also called ervil

indicators.note: the first sign of a word is its initial letter

explanation.surface: A botanist swaps one plant for another at the first hint of spores.
explanation.walkthrough: ERS is an old name for bitter vetch, a fodder plant; zoogonidia are swimming spores.
explanation.definitionFit: Ersatz describes an inferior replacement, a stand-in for the genuine article.

clue.text: Review Vatican City — and in Latin

parts.note: V is the international vehicle registration code for Vatican City
et is the Latin word for and

explanation.surface: An inspection of the papal state, conducted in the Church's language.
explanation.definitionFit: To vet something is to examine or check it carefully before approval.

clue.text: What's Achilles famed for? Virility, and for one bone. Ulna? No no

indicators.note: the outburst No, set beside a second no, is the only hint that the letters are to be rearranged, a very weak signal

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I
the word no taken as written, whose letters are removed from the pool

explanation.surface: A quiz on the hero's fame drifts into anatomy and manliness, with an emphatic denial.
explanation.walkthrough: Pool VIRILITY, BONE and ULNA, take away I (for one) and NO, and rearrange the rest. The blogger found no proper anagram signal; the doubled 'No' is the best candidate.
explanation.definitionFit: Achilles was invulnerable except at his heel, so his famous weak spot makes him a byword for susceptibility to harm.

clue.text: Old coin they're devaluing with bent pin

indicators.note: devaluing suggests the worth being knocked about, so the letters are knocked into another order

explanation.surface: Coin collectors lament a bent pin reducing a coin's worth.
explanation.walkthrough: A threepenny bit was a pre-decimal British coin worth three old pence, withdrawn in 1971.
explanation.definitionFit: This twelve-sided British coin is no longer legal tender, so it counts as an old one.

clue.text: C. American Indian or French N. American native

parts.note: the Carib are an Indigenous people of Central America and the Caribbean
ou is French for or

explanation.surface: A list of Indigenous peoples of the Americas offered with alternatives.
explanation.definitionFit: The reindeer of North America is a native animal there, so it fits the abbreviated definition.

clue.text: Heeled shoe for professional dancers

indicators.note: a ship that has heeled has tipped over, so the letters after it are tipped into a new order

explanation.surface: A high-heeled shoe made for dancers on stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heeled' looks like it describes the shoe; it signals rearranging SHOE FOR.
explanation.definitionFit: Hoofer is informal, chiefly American, slang for a professional dancer, especially a tap or chorus dancer.

clue.text: It's depressing if energy's sapped to be burdened

indicators.note: sapped means drained away, so the letter for energy is drawn out of the word

parts.note: leaden means heavy and gloomy, hence depressing
E is the symbol for energy in physics

explanation.surface: Losing energy is a gloomy business when you are weighed down.
explanation.definitionFit: Laden means loaded or weighed down with something heavy, the same as carrying a burden.

clue.text: It's inevitable English men will be confused with studs

indicators.note: confused means mixed up, so the letters given are jumbled together

explanation.surface: A prediction that Englishmen will be mistaken for stallions.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is short for 'needs must when the devil drives': one must do it, as there is no choice.

clue.text: Such as "You cannot hope to bribe or twist" in club, I report

definitions.text: Such as "You cannot hope to bribe

indicators.note: twist means bend out of shape, so the letters of the clause after it are wrung into a new order

explanation.surface: Quoting Humbert Wolfe's verse about the unbribable British journalist, met at a club.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotation is Humbert Wolfe's 'You cannot hope to bribe or twist, thank God! the British journalist'; 'twist' belongs both to the quote and to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who cannot be bought or corrupted, like Wolfe's journalist, is beyond the reach of bribery.

clue.text: Player against all others is possessive

parts.note: in the game of tag the chaser, who plays against everyone else, is called it
is shortens to 's

explanation.surface: A greedy team-mate who plays against everyone wants to keep the ball.
explanation.definitionFit: This form is the possessive pronoun of 'it', showing belonging, as in 'the dog wagged its tail'.

clue.text: Bird-like model Dior hit on

indicators.note: model as a verb means shape or fashion, so the letters are shaped into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A catwalk model wearing a feathered Dior design catches the eye.
explanation.definitionFit: Ornithoid is a zoological term for something resembling birds in form or structure.

clue.text: Some having it after noon can't, says Burns with grace

definitions.text: Some having it after noon can't, says Burns with grace

parts.words: Some having it after noon can't, says Burns with grace
parts.note: the Selkirk Grace, linked to Robert Burns; the missing word, put after M for noon, makes meat

explanation.surface: A Scots poet's grace says some who have food cannot do what is needed.
explanation.walkthrough: The Selkirk Grace is said before meals, famously at Burns Night suppers. 'Noon' is M, and 'having it after noon' is having meat.
explanation.definitionFit: The grace says some have meat but cannot take food in, which is the verb wanted.

clue.text: Bet it's nice and easy for founder of monasteries

indicators.note: easy here means loose or relaxed, so the letters before it are loosened into a new order

explanation.surface: A gambler's tip that an easy wager on the monk is a good idea.
explanation.definitionFit: Benedict of Nursia wrote the Rule for monastic life and founded Monte Cassino, establishing Western monasticism.

clue.text: Commercial fitting or linking device

parts.note: an ad is a commercial, an advertisement
apt means suitable or fitting

explanation.surface: Choosing between a shop fitting and a coupling device.
explanation.definitionFit: This device joins two parts that would otherwise not connect, such as a plug and a foreign socket.

clue.text: Croon? It's not current and out of fashion, like these musicians

indicators.note: not means without, so the letter for current is removed from the pool
taken as fashion out, meaning shape into something new, so the remaining letters are reshaped

parts.note: I is the physics symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: Crooning has gone out of style, like those old-time players.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove I (current) from CROON IT'S and rearrange the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: A consort is a small group of musicians, such as a consort of viols playing early music.

clue.text: Grant: half the man Jimmy Shand was

indicators.note: half the means take the first half of the word that follows

parts.note: Sir Jimmy Shand was a famous Scottish dance-band leader who played the squeezebox, an accordionist

explanation.surface: A man named Grant compared with a famous bandleader.
explanation.walkthrough: Jimmy Shand (1908-2000) was a Scottish accordion player, hugely popular on radio and TV.
explanation.definitionFit: To accord is to give or bestow, as in 'accord someone an honour'.

clue.text: Goddess born in Cyprus, everybody's first love, when heart is lost

parts.note: CY is the international code for Cyprus

indicators.note: first means take the opening letter of the word it follows
the heart of a word is its central pair of letters, which are dropped here

parts.note: taken as written before its middle is removed

explanation.surface: An island-born goddess of love whose devotees lose heart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when heart is lost' leaves LE from LOVE.
explanation.definitionFit: Cybele was the Phrygian mother goddess, worshipped in Rome as Magna Mater.

clue.text: Jerry for Jocks packs — with difficulty — lace

indicators.note: packs means holds inside, so one piece is stuffed into the other

parts.note: chanty is Scots slang for a chamber pot, which is also called a jerry
ill as an adverb means hardly or with difficulty

explanation.surface: A German soldier, among Scots, struggles with a parcel of lace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jerry' looks like a German but is a chamber pot; Jocks are Scots.
explanation.definitionFit: Chantilly is a delicate bobbin lace named after the French town where it was made.

clue.text: Knowing Nancy tickled

indicators.note: tickled means stirred up playfully, so the letters of the name are stirred into another order

explanation.surface: A worldly girl named Nancy is amused.
explanation.definitionFit: Canny means shrewd or astute, having a sharp understanding of how things work.

clue.text: Prance about (and shortly out?)

indicators.note: about means around or in disorder, so the letters left are moved around
out means removed, so the short form of and is taken away

parts.note: 'n' is the clipped form of and, as in rock 'n' roll

explanation.surface: Dancing around, and perhaps getting cut off quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: Take N from PRANCE and rearrange the rest; the whole clue also describes the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To caper is to skip or leap about playfully, which is what prancing around amounts to.

clue.text: Dependency of character from Uz in Old Testament (Job)

indicators.note: in puts the chosen letter inside the abbreviation for the scripture
a character is a letter, here the first one of the place name

parts.note: a post is a job or position

explanation.surface: Job, the Old Testament figure, came from the land of Uz.
explanation.walkthrough: The Book of Job opens 'There was a man in the land of Uz'; 'Job' here is a job, POST.
explanation.definitionFit: An outpost is a remote settlement or territory under a distant power, a dependency of it.

clue.text: To perform without preparation is failing to make progress

indicators.note: failing means absent or lacking, so the two letters named are missing

parts.note: to improvise is to perform without rehearsal or preparation

explanation.surface: Ad-libbing is no way to get better.
explanation.definitionFit: To get better or develop is to make progress, the intransitive sense of the verb.

clue.text: 50% of 20 or 80 or 90? All the same?

definitions.meaning: written out, twenty, eighty and ninety are six letters each, and the same three letters make up half of every one
a conjunction meaning nevertheless or even so

explanation.surface: A puzzled arithmetic question about percentages, and whether they come out equal.
explanation.walkthrough: TWENTY, EIGHTY and NINETY each contain Y, E and T: half their letters, and the same in all three.
explanation.definitionFit: 'All the same' and this word both mean nevertheless, even so, in spite of that.

clue.text: Mock eiderdown the worse for wear now thrown out

indicators.note: the worse for wear means battered, so the remaining letters are knocked about into a new order
thrown out means discarded, so the letters of the time word are removed

explanation.surface: A tatty old quilt is finally binned.
explanation.walkthrough: Take NOW from EIDERDOWN and rearrange the remaining EIDERD.
explanation.definitionFit: To deride is to ridicule or scoff at, the same as to mock.

clue.text: Move sinuously with sex-appeal. (Fancy her concealing that!)

indicators.note: fancy as an adjective means elaborate or ornamented, so the letters are dressed up in a new order

parts.note: it is old slang for sex appeal, from the 1927 Clara Bow film

explanation.surface: A seductive dancer sways, and the speaker is surprised she hides it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'concealing that' is surface: the blogger takes W, IT and HER as one pool to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: To writhe is to twist and squirm, a sinuous movement of the body.
